rows.question: What kinds of old photos do users struggle to retrieve?
rows.restated: What kinds of old photos do users struggle to retrieve?
problems: evidence: a FULL answer quotes no story
rows.text:
People struggle most with photos they only vaguely remember, across three kinds. [[analysis_funnel|stories:core]] Among photos kept as memories (people, trips, events), 13 of 48 stories (27%) say the search did not understand what they typed, a small group, so only a rough guide. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:sentimental]] Among photos whose post does not say why they were kept, 15 of 46 stories (33%) say the search did not understand what they typed, a small group, so only a rough guide. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:unclear]] Among photos kept for the information in them (receipts, documents, notes), 8 of 21 stories say the photo was already gone. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=0@photo_class:utility]] One limit is that these are public posts. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

*Want a quick summary as a one-liner?*

rows.question: What information do people actually remember about a photo?
rows.restated: What information do people actually remember about a photo?
rows.gap: two AI readers went through the stories separately and agreed too rarely on what they actually remember about the photo to rely on it
rows.text:
These stories cannot reliably tell what people remember about a photo, because two AI readers agreed too rarely on it. [[analysis_reliability|q:2.1]][[analysis_method_flags|no_gold_standard]]

People most often remembered what was in the photo, like the main subject or objects. [[analysis_derived|cue_remembered:what:core]][[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.1=what:main_subject@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.1=what:objects@photo_class:_all]]
Some remembered when it was taken, such as the year. [[analysis_derived|cue_remembered:when:core]][[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.1=when:year@photo_class:_all]]
Others recalled who was in it. [[analysis_derived|cue_remembered:who:core]][[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.1=who:people_present@photo_class:_all]]
One person said they searched the “words on the posters” and found the photo. [[story|90c8b5f8d8913d764335d981d06c5dc02200c937:0]]
One limit is that these are public posts. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

*Want a quick view of which details people forgot most?*

rows.question: What information have people forgotten about the photo they want?
rows.restated: What information have people forgotten about the photo they want?
withheld: unverifiable quote: forgotten what was in it
rows.draft:
People most often forget when the photo was taken. [[analysis_derived|cue_forgotten:when:core]] In 13 of 115 stories (11%) about a photo the person only vaguely remembered, they had forgotten when it was taken. [[analysis_derived|cue_forgotten:when:core]] People also forget the date or year. [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.4=date_or_year@photo_class:_all]] A smaller number forget where it was taken, or the exact place or venue name. [[analysis_derived|cue_forgotten:where:core]][[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.4=exact_place_or_venue_name@photo_class:_all]] A few forget whether it was a photo, video or screenshot, or which app or account it was in. [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.4=photo_video_or_screenshot@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.4=which_app_or_account@photo_class:_all]] One person wrote they had "forgotten what was in it" [[analysis_derived|cue_forgotten:what:core]][[story|eb1a88bd470868f13eabf5ce1386418e831b7917:0]]. One limit is that these are public posts. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

*Want a quick summary of what people still remember?*
rows.text:
- In 13 of 115 stories (11%) about a photo the person only vaguely remembered, on what they have forgotten about the photo, the post says: date or year. [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.4=date_or_year@photo_class:_all]]
- In 4 of 115 stories (3%) about a photo the person only vaguely remembered, on what they have forgotten about the photo, the post says: exact place or venue name. [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.4=exact_place_or_venue_name@photo_class:_all]]
- In 1 of 115 stories (1%) about a photo the person only vaguely remembered, on what they have forgotten about the photo, the post says: photo video or screenshot. [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.4=photo_video_or_screenshot@photo_class:_all]]
- One of the posts this rests on, to read in full [[story|1d58cd6877f9f89ca1ae67d0099128407747c22f:0]]

Every figure counts stories people chose to post in public. It is not a success rate, and not a share of Google Photos users or of searches. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

*Want to ask it more narrowly?*

rows.question: How do users formulate searches when their memory is incomplete?
rows.restated: How do users formulate searches when their memory is incomplete?
rows.text:
People often type a simple thing they remember, like an object or word in the picture. [[analysis_funnel|stories:core]][[story|790de55c9d650cb50647f97841544a0c5b1b7275:0]][[story|90c8b5f8d8913d764335d981d06c5dc02200c937:0]] Many try one plain word first, such as “vomit,” and expect matches; sometimes the search shows nothing. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]][[story|88a83897e2c872e72ac85967d7fc5c158d43bbb0:0]] Some do not use the search box at all and scroll or look elsewhere. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=3@photo_class:_all]] In 38 of 115 stories (33%), nothing went wrong — they found the photo, so these simple searches can work. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=9@photo_class:_all]]

One limit is that these are public posts. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

*Want examples of the words people typed?*

rows.question: Does Google Photos fail to understand the clues people give it?
rows.restated: Does Google Photos fail to understand the clues people give it?
rows.text:
Often, yes — many stories say the search did not understand the words people typed or showed the wrong photos. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]]  
This happened in 31 of 115 stories (27%) about a photo the person only vaguely remembered. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_method_flags|thin_core]]  
One person wrote that typing “dog” returned “too many photos with no dog,” and “dog with black hair” gave no results. [[story|c06874c9c9acadf8038072c41b2d0d2c08c2bc10:0]]  
Still, nothing went wrong in 38 of 115 stories (33%); they found the photo. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=9@photo_class:_all]]  
One limit is that these are public posts. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

*Want examples of the kinds of clues that were missed?*

rows.question: What is Google Photos' annual revenue?
rows.restated: How much annual revenue does Google Photos generate?
rows.gap: these are public stories, not usage data: no rate of success or failure, and no count of users, can be produced from them
rows.text: Google Photos’ annual revenue cannot be reported from these stories; they are public posts about trying to find a photo, and they contain no financial or revenue data for Google Photos or Alphabet. These stories cannot provide a rate of success or failure, and they cannot give any count of users. This question would require audited financial reports or company disclosures, not public anecdotes.

rows.question: Do Android users struggle to find photos more than iPhone users?
rows.restated: Do Android users struggle to find photos more than iPhone users?
rows.gap: the posts do not reliably say which phone people use, so there is no Android vs iPhone split
rows.text:
The stories cannot tell whether Android users struggle more than iPhone users, because they do not contain a reliable field for device platform or user counts. [[analysis_method_flags|missing_cuts]]  
What they can tell is where posts came from: 2,500 posts came from App Store reviews and 2,000 from Google Play reviews. [[analysis_sources|appstore]][[analysis_sources|play]]  
Across all sources, 31,235 public posts, reviews and comments were read, written by 29,314 people. [[analysis_funnel|collected]]  
One person said “IOS Photos does it on specific numbers” when comparing apps. [[story|ac7cfeda39451a237d2ad146b43c59993c4a9c0a:0]]  
One limit is that these are public posts. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

rows.question: Has search got worse since Ask Photos launched?
rows.restated: Has Google Photos search quality declined since the launch of Ask Photos?
rows.gap: the stories were not compared across time, so there is no before-and-after
rows.text:
The stories cannot show before-and-after, so they cannot say whether search got worse after Ask Photos launched. [[analysis_method_flags|missing_cuts]]  
Some stories do say search did not match what people asked for. [[analysis_coverage|5.1]]  
One person wrote that Ask Photos found too few: “I am not seeing great search results with Ask Photos… it only comes up with 5 of them and I have 50+.” [[analysis_coverage|5.6]][[story|b4a4d8c14233f96a727cec35a5c67f19ad91d59a:1]]  
Others say results were unrelated to the words they used. [[analysis_coverage|5.1]][[analysis_coverage|5.6]][[story|ae1d6b3c7301cf80eb893d734de853980634269f:0]][[story|50aee66bc91c783509c972b3f44b764fbf536234:1]]  
One limit is that these are public posts. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

rows.question: Is Apple Photos search better than Google Photos search at finding old photos?
rows.restated: Is Apple Photos search better than Google Photos search at finding old photos?
rows.gap: the stories do not compare how well other photo apps search
rows.text:
Apple Photos is not shown to be better here, because the stories do not compare how well other photo apps search. [[analysis_method_flags|missing_cuts]]  
These are public posts about trying to find a photo, not a measure of any app’s overall performance. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

Some people said search did not understand what they typed: 14 of 49 stories (29%) among x photos — a small group, so only a rough guide. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@source:x]]  
A few people said they did find their photo: 6 of 11 among hackernews photos, and 6 of 8 among quora photos. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=9@source:hackernews]][[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=9@source:quora]]  
One person wrote “I found my old baby photos in this app tysm” [[story|e7e4eb6a20b124405577ba1cd0fa0775014739c9:0]].  

One limit is that people mostly post when something goes wrong. [[analysis_method_flags|public_selection_bias]]

rows.question: Why does Ask Photos fail most often?
rows.restated: Why does Ask Photos fail most often?
rows.text:
Most often, the search does not understand what people type, or it shows the wrong photos. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]]

Fix search understanding first. In 31 of 115 stories (27%) about a photo the person only vaguely remembered, the first thing that went wrong was that search did not understand what they typed, or showed the wrong photos. [[analysis_opportunity|stage5]][[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]] “text search … and be disappointed.” [[story|b2358d9efca162742579284a99c00a353586c178:0]][[analysis_synthesis|recommendation:chain:evidence]] Deletion before any search comes up in 20 of 115 stories (17%). *Want a short list of fixes inside search understanding?*
rows.text:
- The problem — search did not understand or match what they typed — comes up in 31 of 115 stories (27%) about a vaguely remembered photo, from 30 people. It is the one problem with enough stories to rank. [[analysis_opportunity|stage5]]
- The problem — the photo was gone before anyone searched — deleted, never backed up, elsewhere — comes up in 20 of 115 stories (17%) about a vaguely remembered photo, from 20 people. Better search could not fix it. [[analysis_opportunity|stage0]]
- The problem — they never searched — scrolled the timeline or didn't know search could help — comes up in 9 of 115 stories (8%) about a vaguely remembered photo, from 9 people. Too few stories to rank it. [[analysis_opportunity|stage3]]
- One of the posts this rests on, to read in full [[story|beebc7898400af1a0cc9f1ea6c04d016e3940312:0]]

The stories cannot tell you all of this: only 21 stories are about photos kept for the information in them (receipts, documents, notes) — too few (under 30) for a percentage, so only counts are given. [[analysis_method_flags|thin_core]]

- In 8 of 21 stories about a photo the person only vaguely remembered, among photos kept for the information in them (receipts, documents, notes), the first thing that went wrong was that the photo was already gone — deleted, never backed up, or kept somewhere else. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=0@photo_class:utility]]
- One of the posts this rests on, to read in full [[story|ca3c4022164a7f654f61a7dc848d7ecddf0ff90b:0]]

Every figure counts stories people chose to post in public. It is not a success rate, and not a share of Google Photos users or of searches. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

People often say the photo was already gone. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=0@photo_class:utility]] They also say they simply could not remember enough to search for it. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=2@photo_class:utility]] Some say the search did not understand what they typed, or showed the wrong photos. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:utility]] One person wrote “'receipt' returned nothing” about a missing laptop receipt. [[story|probe-inj-04]]

Only 21 stories are about receipts, documents or notes — too few (under 30) for a percentage, so only counts are given. [[analysis_method_flags|thin_core]] One limit is that these are public posts. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

Most often, the search misunderstands what people type, or shows the wrong photos. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]] For stories about a photo the person only vaguely remembered, this happened in 31 of 115 stories (27%). [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=0@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_funnel|stories:core]]
